subject: Accounting
title: Accounts Receivable Management
description: A quick win: understand Accounts Receivable Management.

hook.text: You sold $50,000 worth of goods on credit. Now the hard part: collecting the money.

buildup.text: Accounts receivable tracks money customers owe you—each invoice, due date, and aging period.

discovery.text: An aging report groups receivables by how overdue they are—30, 60, 90, 120+ days.

twist.text: The longer a receivable ages, the less likely it is to be collected. Time is the enemy.

climax.text: Proactive follow-up on overdue accounts keeps cash flowing and bad debts under control.

punchline.text: A sale isn't complete until the cash arrives.

quiz.question: What does an aging report show?
options: How long receivables have been outstanding

details.summary: Accounts receivable management tracks money owed to a business by its customers. This topic covers invoicing, aging analysis, collection strategies, and how receivables management directly impacts a company's cash flow and profitability.
details.whyItMatters: Revenue means nothing if customers don't pay. Effective receivable management ensures that earned revenue actually converts to cash, keeping the business solvent and growing.
takeaways: Accounts receivable represents money customers owe for goods or services already delivered
Aging reports categorize receivables by how long they've been outstanding
The longer a receivable goes unpaid, the less likely it will ever be collected

faq.question: What is accounts receivable management?
faq.answer: Accounts receivable management is the process of tracking customer invoices, monitoring payment timelines, following up on overdue amounts, and maintaining records of what is owed—ensuring that sales on credit actually convert to cash in the bank.

faq.question: How does an accounts receivable aging report work?
faq.answer: An aging report groups outstanding invoices by how long they've been unpaid—typically current, 30 days, 60 days, 90 days, and over 90 days. This helps businesses identify problem accounts early and prioritize collection efforts.
